title: NBA SOTA — LSTM+Brier 0.1589 NCAA + Foresight Learning RL for TF agents

papers.title: Forecasting NCAA Basketball Outcomes with Deep Learning: LSTM and Transformer Models
papers.key_finding: LSTM+Brier loss achieves Brier score 0.1589 on NCAA Division 1 Men's/Women's tournaments. Transformer+BCE achieves AUC 0.8473 (best discrimination). Brier loss explicitly optimizes calibration; BCE optimizes discrimination. Key features: GLM team quality, Elo ratings, seed differences, box-score stats.
papers.actionable: (1) Switch plain xgboost islands to xgboost_brier (already done S15/S18). (2) For GPU burst (Modal A10G/ZeroGPU): try LSTM with Brier loss on full 9551-game NBA dataset. (3) Add Elo rating as explicit feature if not already in engine. Expected gain: 0.02-0.04 Brier improvement on GPU.
papers.relevance: HIGH — same sport domain, same Brier metric. 0.1589 NCAA vs our 0.22019 NBA = 0.062 gap. Direct architecture to try on GPU burst.

papers.title: Future-as-Label: Scalable Supervision from Real-World Outcomes (Foresight Learning)
papers.key_finding: Qwen3-32B trained with RLVR using proper scoring rules (Brier score as reward signal) improves Brier by 27%% and halves calibration error vs pretrained baseline. Outperforms Qwen3-235B (7x larger) on forecasting tasks.
papers.actionable: Apply to TF LLM agents: current agents evaluated on WR and PnL but not explicit Brier score reward. Adding per-day Brier score as RL signal to the agent improvement cycle (tf_improvement_cycle.py) could fix measured agent Brier=0.41. This is the key paper for the probation/Kelly system — agents trained on Brier RLVR would self-calibrate without needing manual probation caps.
papers.relevance: HIGH — directly applicable to TF LLM agent calibration problem (Brier 0.41 → target <0.28).

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for NBA Forecasting in Digital Betting Markets
papers.key_finding: LSTM with Monte Carlo dropout provides calibrated probability estimates. Most influential features: home indicator, team Elo ratings, next-game information (days rest). Isotonic calibration post-processing shown effective.
papers.actionable: Add next_game_days_rest as feature candidate if not already present. Monte Carlo dropout requires GPU (Modal/ZeroGPU). Isotonic calibration already in our best model (0.22054).
papers.relevance: MEDIUM — NBA specific but GPU-dependent for LSTM/MC-dropout

papers.title: Rethinking Evaluation Metric for Probability Estimation: Balance Score
papers.key_finding: Balance Score proposed as superior alternative to Brier+ECE. Approximates true expected calibration error without binning artifacts.
papers.actionable: Add Balance Score metric to tf_rigorous_validation.py alongside existing Brier/ECE. Gives cleaner calibration signal for agent evaluation.
papers.relevance: LOW-MEDIUM — evaluation enhancement, no training change
